ra: Baubo is part of the Eleusinian cult cast (the iambe/jesting episode of the Homeric Hymn to Demeter).
Eumolpus is the legendary founding hierophant of the Eleusinian Mysteries and eponym of the Eumolpidai.
Demophoon's immortalization episode is a foundational Eleusinian narrative.
Daeira received her own priestess and sacrifices within the Eleusinian cult complex.
Demeter is the principal goddess of the Eleusinian Mysteries.
Persephone (Kore) is the central abducted-and-returned goddess of the Eleusinian cult.
Demeter nurses the infant Demophoon and attempts to immortalize him in the Homeric Hymn to Demeter.
Baubo's obscene jesting consoles the grieving Demeter at Eleusis.
Ancient sources variously identify the Eleusinian Daeira with Persephone.
Eumolpus and Triptolemus are paired Eleusinian founder-heroes in Athenian tradition.
Axieros is a named member of the Samothracian Great Gods tetrad.
Axiokersa is a named member of the Samothracian Great Gods tetrad.
Axiokersos is a named member of the Samothracian Great Gods tetrad.
Kadmilos/Kasmilos is the fourth named member of the Samothracian Great Gods tetrad.
The tetrad collectively constitutes the existing Great Gods of Samothrace.
Axiokersa is one of the existing Great Gods of Samothrace.
Axiokersos is one of the existing Great Gods of Samothrace.
Kadmilos is one of the existing Great Gods of Samothrace.
Kadmilos is closely linked to the Cabeiri as their attendant/father-figure in the Samothracian-Cabiric tradition.
Ancient interpretatio (scholia to Apollonius) identifies the Samothracian Axieros with Demeter.
Axieros as the Samothracian Great Mother was also identified with the Cybele-type Mother of the Gods.
Ancient scholia identify the Samothracian Axiokersa with Persephone.
Ancient scholia identify the Samothracian Axiokersos with Hades.
Ancient scholia identify the Samothracian Kadmilos/Kasmilos with Hermes.
The 'Most High God' cult-title often attached to Zeus (Zeus Hypsistos) in pagan dedications across the Roman East.
The Theos Hypsistos / Hypsistarian cult partly converged with the worship of the Jewish God among God-fearers, blurring pagan and Jewish monotheizing devotion.
